extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: A 1.2 million-sized open-data SFT reasoning dataset composed of math, code, and science datapoints, built through a pipeline of sourcing questions, filtering questions, deduplicating some domains, sampling questions, and generating multiple answers with a teacher model.
extraction.creator: OpenThoughts project team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by sourcing many questions in math, code, and science, filtering questions, deduplicating math and science questions, randomly sampling questions, and generating multiple answers per question with a teacher model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from existing datasets, online forums, competition sites, textbooks/PDFs, and synthetic generation pipelines across math, code, and science domains.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered, math and science questions were deduplicated, questions were randomly sampled, multiple answers were generated per question, and datasets were decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Responses/reasoning traces were generated by teacher models for each question; the final pipeline uses QwQ-32B as the teacher model and 16 answers per question for all domains.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors compared answer filtering and verification strategies and concluded that no answer filtering strategy outperformed using all answers, so they skipped answer filtering in the final pipeline.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05, fastText
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Question quality and source selection strongly affect downstream performance, and optimizing for a small number of high-quality sources performed better than maximizing diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The work did not explore reinforcement learning datasets, staged SFT, or curriculum learning, and selected strategies by maximizing overall average benchmark performance rather than optimizing each domain individually.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training / supervised fine-tuning of reasoning models.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our full dataset begins with sourcing many questions in math, code, and science domains. The next step is filtering those questions, deduplicating the math and science questions, randomly sampling questions, and then generating multiple answers for each question.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We can broadly categorize our question sourcing techniques into three types: (1) Fully synthetic – an existing LLM generates questions with little-to-no seed material... (2) Semi-synthetic – an LLM uses existing data sources such as CommonCrawl or FineWeb as seeds to form questions... (3) Non-synthetic – humans write the questions. Examples include StackExchange and ShareGPTCode. These questions often arise from online forums, contests, chatbot interactions, and other sources.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Our full dataset begins with sourcing many questions in math, code, and science domains. The next step is filtering those questions, deduplicating the math and science questions, randomly sampling questions, and then generating multiple answers for each question. We also decontaminate our datasets against our benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Takeaway: Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains. ... Takeaway: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Takeaway: We do not perform answer filtering because no filtering strategy outperformed the baseline, which uses all the answers.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Takeaway: Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Takeaway: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model. We use GPT-4o-mini for all sources that we generate which require an LLM. Takeaway: We use difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions. We test different LLMs such as GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-nano for response length filtering. We use gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 with the prompt in Figure 24 to extract the text from the PDFs. We extensively explore various filtering methods, including fastText classifiers, difficulty scores, and embedding distance, to select higher-quality questions.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Selecting questions from a small number (top 1 or 2) of high-quality sources leads to better downstream performance compared to optimizing for diversity (i.e., top 8 or 16 sources).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: This work has several limitations. We did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning, a standard training regime for building reasoning models. Within the SFT realm, we did not explore the use of staged SFT or curriculum learning to further improve performance.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Training Our goal is to create the best dataset of question-response pairs for SFT reasoning.
